title: Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services

reading.body:
AI-generated video and deepfake technology were used to create a fraudulent impersonation of a real attorney. Scammers deployed hundreds of fake social media accounts across multiple platforms using synthetic media of the attorney's likeness to solicit payment for immigration services. The fraud targeted a vulnerable population, immigrants seeking legal assistance, and succeeded because the synthetic videos appeared credible enough to convince victims to send money.

The deployment failure was at the social media platforms themselves. Facebook, TikTok, and Instagram each hosted thousands of fraudulent accounts impersonating a specific named individual before they were removed by a hired anti-piracy company. The platforms did not catch the accounts through their own systems or before real financial harm occurred. What would have caught this: either verification systems that confirm accounts claiming to offer legal services, or detection of the same likeness being impersonated across multiple accounts at scale.

It is not established whether the AI video generation was done by the scammers themselves or purchased as a service, or what specific detection opportunities the platforms missed.

reports.title: Scammers steal identity of renowned Miami attorney to target immigrants on social media
South Florida immigration attorney says AI scammers are using his identity to target immigrants
Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services
Legal resident loses thousands seeking citizenship to AI immigration attorney

summary:
Angel Leal, a South Florida immigration attorney with over 30 years of experience, has become the target of an artificial intelligence fraud scheme. Scammers have created hundreds of fake social media profiles and AI-generated videos using his likeness to trick vulnerable immigrants into paying thousands of dollars for immigration services he never offered. In one video, a digital version of Leal promises US residency assistance for $2,200 to undocumented immigrants without deportation orders. Leal discovered the scam when potential clients began calling his office about services he did not provide.

The fraud has dramatically escalated over the past three months, though Leal first noticed suspicious activity in October. His office hired an anti-piracy company that has removed nearly 6,500 fake profiles, including 3,500 from TikTok, 2,400 from Facebook, and 544 from Instagram. The scammers direct victims through WhatsApp and send fake contracts before requesting payment via Venmo, Zelle, or Cash App. Leal has changed his personal phone number and plans to contact local and federal authorities to investigate the scheme. He warns immigrants to verify anyone offering legal services online and avoid anyone requesting immediate payment through social media.
